req.title: Basic-auth requires both segments
req.statement: The system shall route /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> only when both user and passwd segments are provided.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> must only route when BOTH path segments are present. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — valid credentials supplied for both segments returns 200 with correct JSON payload; (2) negative NEG — missing passwd segment causes 404 (route not matched); (3) negative NEG — missing both segments causes 404; (4) DT — wrong credentials returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate header; (5) BVA — single-character user and passwd at the minimal boundary; (6) DT — correct user but wrong passwd returns 401 (boolean AND in check_basic_auth); (7) EP — correct passwd but wrong user returns 401. These collectively kill mutations on the equality checks in check_basic_auth, the route pattern, and the status_code branching.

tests.name: test_basic_auth_valid_credentials_returns_200_with_payload
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Both user and passwd path segments are provided
Correct Basic Auth credentials are sent
actions: Send GET /basic-auth/myuser/mypass with Authorization: Basic base64(myuser:mypass)
expected: JSON body contains authenticated=true and user='myuser'
trace: R-HTTPBIN-049: both segments provided -> route matched -> check_basic_auth passes -> 200
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()
creds = base64.b64encode(b'myuser:mypass').decode('ascii')
headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'}
r = client.get('/basic-auth/myuser/mypass', headers=headers)
assert r.status_code == 200
data = r.get_json()
assert data['authenticated'] == True
assert data['user'] == 'myuser'

def test_basic_auth_valid_credentials_returns_200_with_payload():
    client = app.test_client()
    creds = base64.b64encode(b'myuser:mypass').decode('ascii')
    headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'}
    r = client.get('/basic-auth/myuser/mypass', headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data['authenticated'] == True
    assert data['user'] == 'myuser'

tests.name: test_basic_auth_response_json_user_field_matches_path_segment
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Both path segments provided with distinct values
Correct credentials sent
actions: Send GET /basic-auth/testuser/testpass with correct Authorization header
expected: JSON authenticated field is exactly True (boolean)
JSON user field is exactly 'testuser' (not 'testpass' or any other value)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-049: EP — verifies jsonify(authenticated=True, user=user) returns correct field values; catches mutation swapping user/passwd or flipping authenticated
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()
creds = base64.b64encode(b'testuser:testpass').decode('ascii')
headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'}
r = client.get('/basic-auth/testuser/testpass', headers=headers)
assert r.status_code == 200
data = r.get_json()
assert data['authenticated'] is True
assert data['user'] == 'testuser'
assert data['user'] != 'testpass'
assert set(data.keys()) == {'authenticated', 'user'}

def test_basic_auth_response_json_user_field_matches_path_segment():

    headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'}
    r = client.get('/basic-auth/testuser/testpass', headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data['authenticated'] is True
    assert data['user'] == 'testuser'
    assert data['user'] != 'testpass'
    assert set(data.keys()) == {'authenticated', 'user'}
